In Hotels With Great Taste, we’re pulling back the curtain for a peek at the “special sauce” that hotels use to create memorable, meaningful culinary experiences for their guests.

Look closely at the lodgings that make up Dawn Ranch and you’ll notice they’re actually a patchwork of historic structures in different shapes and sizes. Each building at the luxe 15-acre Russian River resort, which is nestled amongst the towering redwoods in the petite town of Guerneville, California, is linked to a different era of the property’s past.

Built in 1905, it was originally Murphy’s Ranch, a getaway for well-to-do families that operated for seven decades. Later it served for more than 20 years as the pioneering gay resort Fife’s. Today, it’s a refined wine country escape that exists at the crossroads of nature and high-end luxury. The hotel is situated in a floodway, which limits construction for safety purposes, so since 1993 the site’s various owners haven’t been able to build anew; renovating ad infinitum has proven to be just dandy though.

In fact, this limitation turns out to be central to Dawn Ranch’s retro, summer camp-adjacent charm, which feels like a happy throwback even with its modernized facilities and amenities. Spectacularly refurbished in 2023, the current upscale iteration features 81 California-cool rooms, a tremendous spa, a fine-dining restaurant that may very well become impossible to book once word gets out, and a thoughtful, dynamic wine program that highlights some of the world’s most unique bottles.

Rachel Tepper Paley

Rachel Tepper Paley

The property and rooms

When it comes to bunking, you have choices that span a hodgepodge of rustic-chic cabins, chalets, cottages, bungalows, and glamping tents. On the main campus, cabins are cozy and compact, while the cottages and chalets offer more space. Most include private outdoor decks, equally ideal for taking in a morning cuppa or an evening tipple. The bungalows are the roomiest accommodation, outfitted for families and large groups with two bedrooms, two baths, a full kitchen, and gas fireplaces. Across the street, the resort’s Grove campus offers more options, which range from snug single-room affairs to spacious two bedrooms.

They’re all scattered amongst the tree-filled property’s sycamores and redwoods, so traipsing to your room feels like a walk in the forest. Inside, the aesthetic is a study in NorCal quiet luxury, with plenty of smooth blonde wood, layered textiles, and eclectic furniture pieces, plus Parachute linens and Le Labo bath goodies.

More adventurous guests will appreciate the smartly furnished glamping tents, situated in Dawn Ranch’s 120-year-old apple tree orchard. The walls may be canvas, but the beds feature the same Bear hybrid mattresses as those in Dawn Ranch’s more conventional rooms. You will, however, have to share a bathhouse—albeit an extremely nice one—with your fellower glampers.

No matter where you sleep, make sure you lay eyes on the resort’s namesake, a 70-year-old pair of rare dawn redwoods located near the pool on the main campus.

The restaurants and dining experience

The Lodge at Dawn Ranch, which houses the hotel’s main dining, bar, and lounge areas, manages a laid-back vibe that nonetheless feels rarefied and celebratory, with plush mauve-colored banquettes and dim romantic lighting.

But food is the real draw: Co-executive chefs (and husband-and-wife team) Ignacio “Nacho” Zuzulich and Juliana Thorpe center a nine-course, $155 tasting menu informed both by their respective Argentinian and Brazilian backgrounds and their experience cooking in lauded kitchens from Mugaritz in Spain to Napa Valley’s Meadowood resort. A truncated version of the tasting menu is served at the bar for $90.

Seasonal Golden State ingredients take top billing. On a recent visit, corn was a standout, taking the form of a delicate tostada set atop a fire-roasted corn custard. Festooned with the marigold-like flowering herb huacatay, it conveyed an impossibly large, flawless lobe of Santa Barbara uni.

In the morning, don’t skip breakfast at the Lodge, which is best taken on the sprawling outside deck. Soft scrambled eggs with avocado and furikake on homemade brioche are straightforward but deeply effective, while the cinnamon rolls glossed in cream cheese frosting are the perfect excuse to eat dessert before noon.

Rachel Tepper Paley

Rachel Tepper Paley

The inside scoop

When drinking, whether in the dining room or bar, vino is the move. This is wine country, after all. The handwritten “Sommelier’s Notebook” dispenses with formality, breaking wines into playful categories like “The Wild Ones,” “Extrovert Whites,” and “Quiet Elegance.” You’ll have plenty of fun ordering by the bottle or glass; if you’re after just a taste, some offerings are available in one-ounce pours.

But for the deep-pocketed, the $400 Decades Wine Pairing is a voyage through time and space, guiding you through wines bottled across generations. The offerings frequently shift, but this past summer, the oldest pour was an intensely molasses-forward D'Oliveiras Verdelho Madeira, first put under cork in 1891.

With its decadent syrup-like texture and vibrant acidity, the Madeira made for a complex complement to the tasting menu’s show-stopping dessert course, which presented local peaches in three manners: a quenelle of peach sorbet; a crystal cupful of peach nectar; and a tart of roasted peach jam and white chocolate ganache, topped with intricately woven, paper-thin peach slivers and served alongside a peach sabayon.

Best of all, returning to my cottage after dinner required only a brief, tipsy walk through the redwoods, the stars lighting my way.

Rachel Tepper Paley

This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews.

Now Open is a yearlong series celebrating some of 2026’s most exciting new restaurants. Throughout the year, we’ll check in with teams in Chicago, New York City, and Washington, D.C., to hear what it’s really like behind the scenes of a buzzy opening. Then, we’ll host exclusive meals at these restaurants as part of Dinner Party, presented by Capital One. Read along for challenges, candid reflections, and advice from the proprietors behind some of the country’s hottest new openings.

Zubair Mohajir is one of Chicago’s most prolific new chefs and restaurateurs, behind such openings as Lilac Tiger, Mariela, Mirra, Sarima, and most recently, Muhājir, a restaurant that traces historical spice routes to tell the story of global migration. I talked to Mohajir about how the opening is going, how he thinks about collaboration across his different projects, and why Muhājir is finally the restaurant that feels like home.

Pre Shift: What did you want to explore with Muhājir that you hadn’t been able to do yet with your previous restaurants?

Zubair Mohajir: Muhājir is such a personal story for me, because my last name is Mohajir, and the meaning of “muhājir” in Arabic and Urdu is “one who migrates.” When the partition [of India and Pakistan] happened, the Muslims that were moved from India to Pakistan were named Muhājirs because they were migrated. In my family, we always wondered why that was our last name. When I started cooking [after working in finance], it really started to settle in. Our late maternal grandfather was obsessed with mapping where this family name came from. It comes from Southern Basra, Iraq, and that was so mind-blowing for me because it’s one of the biggest spice roads.

At Coach House for the past five years, I’ve been exploring ancient recipes in southern Spain and southern Portugal. [They] bring in pre-Crusade Muslim, Christian, Jewish [influences] that are also affected by the Southeast Asian traders coming on the spice road that shoots through the Mediterranean and hits North Africa and the Iberian Peninsula. I’m just obsessed with history and it started to become very evident for me that I really wanted to feed people, but with the context of where the food came from.

At Muhājir, it’s all about riding the spice road that runs from Portugal through the Mediterranean, through the Levantine [region], and then hits out of Basra, Iraq, into the Persian Gulf, and the first landmass it comes across is southern India, where I’m from. We’re all muhājirs — you know, all of our families came from somewhere, and that really has been the driving force for me.

Why did you decide to build the restaurant around live fire?

I’d never cooked on live fire, but we’re cooks, and it was going back to core things. I remember growing up in my grandmother’s house back home in India, and it’s not like there were gas stoves everywhere. When I decided that I was going to do Muhājir, it became so obvious to me that it couldn’t just be a sauté pan on a stove. The story that we wanted to tell had to be told through wood fire.

Is there a dish that feels especially representative of Muhājir?

We do a duck that is inspired by a 927-year-old recipe we found from southern Spain that is influenced by Roman garums, Muslim origins, and Jewish origins. We do this duck “experience,” where we take a whole duck, butcher it, and have the crown dry-aging for seven days. We take the wings and make a jus [and] take the legs and make a confit. We blast that duck crown over the fire when we start service every day, and then it gets finished in the brasa. If you’re sitting in the restaurant, you can see the ducks hanging over the fire.

When we present it, we have this beautiful ornate Turkish platter. There’s black raspberry achaar, the duck jus in a saucier, the duck rice next to it, the duck skin cut in these beautiful medallions on top almost like duck chicharrón, and then we’re also presenting the duck breast itself that has a very crispy skin. The top of that duck breast is the spice mix from that exact recipe that’s more than 900 years old, with cumin, coriander, cardamom, toasted pine nuts, red wine vinegar, and fish sauce. It’s a story of cross-cultural collaboration.

You have a bar called Bobo behind the restaurant. How do the two spaces complement each other?

Bobo’s really inspired by Jacob Dela Cruz, who’s my partner here. We built Sarima together, and it became very important to me to highlight his upbringing and his background as well. He was one who said, “You should name the restaurant Muhājir.” His point was that we’re all immigrants. I was like, “That’s such a simple statement, but such a profound statement.” It was kind of vice versa when we were talking about the bar: Jacob’s father is an amazing person and his name is Bho, and “bobo” in Tagalog means “silly” or “stupid,” as a term of endearment. We always say that as Spice Road-driven and transformative the food experience at Muhājir is, we still like to have fun.

If people are early for their reservation, we take them back to Bobo, or they stop by after dinner. You can’t get to Bobo without walking through the restaurant, so the spaces contribute to each other. If you came to Bobo, you might be like, “I want to eat there.” And if you come straight to Muhājir and see people walking back constantly, you might be like, “What’s happening back there?”

What has it been like to run Muhājir so far?

I wouldn’t say it’s easier [than my other restaurants], but now I don’t freak out. I’ve created a methodical way of approaching issues or problems head-on and figuring it out as a group or with the people that support us. We don’t have investors who are private equity firms; our investors are our guests. When it comes to managing expectations and navigating obstacles, you get better with repetition.

I’m living a dream. Sometimes, when you’re building restaurants with others, you’re not necessarily in the kitchen. [At Mirra, I] was like, “I’m helping create and build this concept, but that’s [chef Rishi Kumar’s] kitchen to run.” Here, it’s the home that I’ve been yearning for and working toward my whole career. I plan to be old in this place. Things have been so crazy and wild and amazing, but slowly, every day, I sit more and more in that moment where I’m like, “This is home.”

This interview has been edited and condensed.

In her pristine Los Angeles kitchen, Nora Lum—the actor, comedian, and rapper better known as Awkwafina—is standing over a stove with two burners and losing the fight with both. Ramen boils on one; Spam violently sizzles over the other. Surveying the spectacle over FaceTime, her nonagenarian grandmother, Powah, cackles and tells her (lovingly) that it looks like shit.

This scene opens Lum’s new show, Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook.

“Food is so important to being Asian,” she announces to the camera. “You can’t talk about being Asian without food being the thread that pulls it all together.” But what if, like the 38-year-old Lum, you can’t even steam an egg?

Family history complicates the answer further. Raised in Forest Hills, NY, the actor has considerable Queens cred (after all, her Comedy Central show was called Awkwafina Is Nora From Queens), but she is also descended from local restaurant royalty.

In 1952 her great-grandfather Jimmy Lum opened the family’s Chinese restaurant in Flushing, one of the first in the neighborhood at the time. “If you lived in New York, not just Queens, at a certain era, almost 10 out of 10 times, you remember Lum’s,” she says. (When I ask some of the food-world old heads I know about it, they respond immediately with memories of the pupu platter, the lobster egg rolls, and the glitzy, neon-lit decor.)

“I’ll cook for a chef any day. With my family, I’ll order out.”

Nora Lum aka Awkwafina, at Bistro Na's in Los Angeles.Photograph by Pat Martin

Lum, who is half Korean, previously explored her mother’s roots on an episode of No Taste Like Home With Antoni Porowski, but she knows little firsthand about her father’s family restaurant, which closed before she was born. “When they talk about it, it’s like they’re talking about a long-lost family member,” she says.

The Apple TV docuseries follows Lum as she meets and cooks with Asian American chefs and restaurateurs. Many of them are like her, restaurant kids who left and eventually found their way back on their own terms. “A lot of their families did not want them to go into the industry. They’re subverting the stereotype in a way,” she says of chefs like Cory Ng and Zhan Chen of NYC's Potluck Club, who help her resurrect Lum’s as a one-night pop-up.

“I always dreamed of being the intrepid restaurant worker,” Lum says. But her family’s attitude toward cooking was less romantic. “Whether it was dishes or cooking, no one trusted me with it. I convinced myself that I’m just not a cook.”

Zigzagging the country changed that, from blowing up a duck at Mister Jiu’s in San Francisco to manning the wok at the Culinary Institute of America in New York to touring Texas barbecue joints with her friend and fellow comedian Jimmy O. Yang. They stopped by Curry Boys BBQ in San Antonio, where traditional Texas brisket is served atop a bowl of green Thai curry, followed by Eaker Barbecue in Fredericksburg for bulgogi sausage. “Seeing Asian people in this environment that’s so Texas, where the two cultures are very different,” broadened her perception of how chefs layer their influences in a way that wasn’t a compromise.

The pleasure of the show is watching Lum encounter new experiences. At a whole-hog barbecue in a Hawaii-set episode, chef Mark Noguchi tells her they’re going to use an imu, an underground pit oven. She lights up, not missing a beat. “Like the bird?”

Her ignorance is played for laughs but is also the source of the show’s unusual tenderness. Lum is game for almost anything, even when she has no idea what is happening. “It’s like one of those school nightmares where you hadn’t completed the class and then you’re just walking in for the test,” she says.

items.text:
Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city. Though it’s somewhat sprawling, the city boasts stunning architecture, incredible food, and an energetic nightlife that stretches until dawn. Over 10 million people visit the city each year, and the minute you step out to explore, you’ll understand why Madrid is one of Europe’s top destinations.


Like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow. It’s a city for night owls, where dinner starts late and the parties even later. But if you can embrace the laid-back pace of life, the slow meals, and the late-night vibes, you’ll have a more authentic visit and uncover the true beating heart of the city’s culture.


I love all my visits to Madrid. I’ve been a few times over the years and the city never ceases to amaze me. The food, the energy, the art (so much art!). Madrid is just cool.


Being such a big city, I know it can be easy to feel lost. Where do you start with what you want to do? Where do you go? It took me a few visits to figure it out.


In this post, I’ll help you plan an epic five-day visit to Madrid that will ensure you not only see the main sights but that you also get off the beaten path and see just what makes Madrid so popular — and all without breaking the bank either!

Day 1: Immersion in the Art Walk


This first day focuses on a prestigious area designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021. There are over 40 monuments and over 40 buildings on the site. It’s easily one of the most picturesque and historic areas of the city.


The route begins at the Prado Museum, one of the best museums on the planet. Here you’ll find works from El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya, as well as many other masters (such as Rubens, Botticelli, and Caravaggio to name a few). If you only visit one museum in Madrid, this is the one. It’s incredible and worth taking the time to explore. It’s one of the biggest museums in the world, too. Make sure you spend a few hours here at a minimum.


Just a 10-minute walk along the Paseo del Prado, the journey continues at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, a private collection spanning from the Renaissance to Pop Art, and culminates at the Reina Sofía Museum. The Reina Sofía National Art Center offers a fantastic collection of modern art. Works by masters like Picasso, Miró, Kandinsky, Dalí, and Bacon can all be found here. The centerpiece is Picasso’s famous Guernica, a 1937 oil painting considered the most moving anti-war painting in the world. While I don’t love modern art, even I enjoyed this museum.


After museum hopping, it’s time to dive into Madrid’s culinary scene. Try Taberna La Fragua de Vulcano for a rustic atmosphere perfect for sampling cocido madrileño. If you are near the Reina Sofía Museum, don’t miss the vibrant garden terrace at Arzábal, renowned for having some of the best croquetas in the city. Finally, for a unique setting, Bodega de los Secretos lets you dine in restored 17th-century wine caves, making it the most atmospheric choice near the Prado Museum.


After a late lunch, spend some time exploring Madrid’s unique ‘House Museums. These are former private palaces that preserve the intimate atmosphere of their original owners. The crown jewel of this collection is the Sorolla Museum, the sun-drenched former residence of ‘the painter of light.’ Following a major architectural renovation, this underrated museum is set to reopen its doors in 2026, offering a refreshed look at its stunning gardens and Mediterranean canvases.


Or if you want something else, there is also the nearby Museum of Romanticism, where you can enjoy a coffee in its secret garden, or visit the Lázaro Galdiano Museum to marvel at a private collection of Goya, Murillo, Velázquez, El Greco, or Bosch housed in a magnificent neo-Renaissance mansion.


In the evening, enjoy some food and relaxation.


Day 2: The Grandeur of the Historic Center


The second day delves into the medieval and Renaissance layout of the city, famously known as Habsburg Madrid (Madrid de los Austrias). The central hub is Puerta del Sol, where a photo at Kilometer Zero and the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue are mandatory for a traveler’s geographic check-in. Kilometer Zero is the official starting point of all the highways and railways in the country, making this effectively the center of the entire country. There’s a small plaque you can snap a photo of.


Nearby is the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue (El Oso y el Madroño). The statue shows a bear reaching up to eat fruit from a madroño tree, symbols which come from Madrid’s coat of arms (the bear represents the city and the tree represents the land and nature surrounding it that has helped make it prosper).


From here, walk toward the iconic Plaza Mayor, highlighting its porticoed architecture and the Casa de la Panadería. Plaza Mayor once hosted bullfights, markets, symphonies, tournaments, and even executions. Now it’s ringed with tourist shops, cafés, and restaurants. It’s a good place from which to indulge in some people-watching, offers some good (though overpriced) bars, and occasionally has concerts and events.


For a true “Local Life” experience, stop for a calamari sandwich in the nearby alleys. Your taste buds will thank you.


After a relaxing lunch and some people watching, head to the Royal Palace of Madrid. The largest palace in Western Europe, the Baroque-style palace was built in the 18th century and is home to over 3,400 lavishly decorated rooms. It was originally built on a former 9th-century Muslim fort and today functions much like an art museum with numerous works, including pieces by Caravaggio, Juan de Flandes, and Francisco Goya. Though it’s the official residence of the royal family, they don’t actually live here anymore, and the palace is only used for official state functions. You can walk through the palace (both self-guided and guided tours are available), starting at the grand stairway, and wander through lavishly decorated staterooms. There’s also the Royal Armory, which houses a collection of medieval weapons and armor.


To end the day, head to the Almudena Cathedral. Unlike many of the famous medieval churches in Europe, this one was constructed in the late 19th century. It was finally completed in 1993 and was consecrated by Pope John Paul II. While the exterior has a Neo-Classical design (to match the nearby palace), the cathedral also has a Neo-Romanesque crypt with over 400 columns that you can explore. Be sure to head up to the dome for stunning views out over the city.


Day 3: Culinary Discovery


Madrid is a paradise for foodies. It’s one of the reasons I keep coming back. While there are plenty of food tours to take in Madrid, I suggest heading off on your own to explore. Begin at the city’s iconic gastronomic markets. The glass-walled Mercado de San Miguel is a must for gourmet tapas near Plaza Mayor. It’s popular with the after-work crowd and is a place I usually visit a few times on my trips. Additionally, local favorites like Mercado de San Antón in Chueca and Mercado de Vallehermoso offer a deeper dive into regional flavors. Just make sure to bring an appetite.


If you do want to take a food tour, consider doing a food tour. This post has more of my suggestions.


For dinner, head to Sobrino de Botín, officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest restaurant. It was actually a favorite of Ernest Hemingway during his time in Madrid. For a more casual vibe, go ‘tapas crawling’ through the historic streets of La Latina or Barrio de las Letras.


As the sun sets, head to the Gran Vía to experience Madrid’s world-class rooftop culture. Venues like The Roof at Picalagartos or RIU, 360º sky bar offer signature cocktails and dinner with breathtaking 360-degree views of the skyline.


For those who don’t eat meat, Madrid has actually evolved into one of Europe’s best veg hubs, boasting a vibrant vegetarian and vegan scene in neighborhoods like Malasaña, where plant-based versions of traditional Spanish dishes are now a staple of the city’s diverse culinary identity.


Day 4: UNESCO World Heritage Wonders


Madrid is the only European capital where nature, science, and royal history converge in a UNESCO World Heritage oasis known as the ‘Paisaje de la Luz‘ (Landscape of Light). But this prestigious area, encompassing the iconic El Retiro Park and the Paseo del Prado, is just the beginning of Spain’s monumental legacy. For more UNESCO wonders, take a day trip out of the city.


One popular destination worth visiting is the Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, a sprawling imperial masterpiece recognized by UNESCO for its historical significance. El Escorial is located just one hour from the city by car and was commissioned by Philip II in the 16th century. It’s a massive palatial complex that includes a monastery, library, palace, basilica, and tomb for Spanish monarchs. Yet as massive as it is, it feels more austere than other palatial complexes, likely owing to its granite walls and symmetrical layout.


Another option for a day trip is the Royal Palace and Gardens of Aranjuez, a World Heritage Cultural Landscape that rivals the beauty of Versailles. Located just one hour south of the city, this was originally a hunting lodge, also commissioned in the 16th century by Philip II. It’s a blend of Renaissance and Baroque styles, with lavish rooms filled with tapestries, porcelain, and ornate decorations. There is lots of greenery and gardens here, which is partly why the royal family used this as their spring residence.


Lastly, there’s the historic university city of Alcalá de Henares, the birthplace of Spanish novelist, poet, and playwright Cervantes (he wrote Don Quixote). Just 45 minutes away by car, it also holds its own UNESCO World Heritage status, offering a perfectly preserved look into the Spanish Golden Age (1492–1659).


Day 5: Off-the-Beaten-Path Treasures


On your last day, it’s time to get further off the beaten path. Step back into the Golden Age at the Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales and the nearby Royal Monastery of La Encarnación, two hidden palaces that house breathtaking royal art collections behind their cloistered walls.


The Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales is a convent founded in 1559 by Joanna of Austria (sister of Philip II). The name “Descalzas Reales” (which means “Royal Barefoot Ladies”) refers to the Order of Saint Clare nuns who lived here in relative austerity. What makes this monastery unique is that many aristocratic women took refuge here, often bringing their artworks and other valuables. Over the years, this turned the convent into a veritable treasure trove of art.


The Royal Monastery of La Encarnación was founded in 1611 by the wife of Philip III, Margaret of Austria. It was a royal convent, meaning it had the direct support of the monarchy. While the exterior has an austere Baroque style, the interior is quite lavish, with ornate chapels, colorful frescoes, and lots of religious sculptures and paintings. It’s also home to several notable relics, including a vial said to contain the blood of Saint Januarius. While tours are available, it’s still an active convent so parts are not open to the public (which, honestly, makes it all the more interesting to see).


To end your day with a local touch, head to the vast Casa de Campo park. This is the largest public park in the city, created in 1931. It covers a whopping 17 square kilometers (6.5 square miles) and includes an artificial lake, lots of paths, a zoo, and even an amusement park. Here, you can enjoy a scenic lunch or dinner at one of the lakeside terraces, offering an unrivaled view of the Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral across the skyline. It’s the perfect place to end your trip.


***


While Barcelona tends to get more attention, I think Madrid is one of the best cities in Europe. It boasts a mouthwatering culinary scene, a raucous nightlife, and tons of things to see and do — no matter your interest or budget. I’ve been visiting the city for almost two decades and never get tired of the tapas, architecture, and history. The city just packs so much in and there really is something for everyone here. By following the itinerary above, you’ll see all the main sights while also getting off the beaten path in Spain’s historic capital.

What makes this monastery unique is that many aristocratic women took refuge here, often bringing their artworks and other valuables. Over the years, this turned the convent into a veritable treasure trove of art.

The Royal Monastery of La Encarnación was founded in 1611 by the wife of Philip III, Margaret of Austria. It was a royal convent, meaning it had the direct support of the monarchy. While the exterior has an austere Baroque style, the interior is quite lavish, with ornate chapels, colorful frescoes, and lots of religious sculptures and paintings. It’s also home to several notable relics, including a vial said to contain the blood of Saint Januarius. While tours are available, it’s still an active convent so parts are not open to the public (which, honestly, makes it all the more interesting to see).

To end your day with a local touch, head to the vast Casa de Campo park. This is the largest public park in the city, created in 1931. It covers a whopping 17 square kilometers (6.5 square miles) and includes an artificial lake, lots of paths, a zoo, and even an amusement park. Here, you can enjoy a scenic lunch or dinner at one of the lakeside terraces, offering an unrivaled view of the Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral across the skyline. It’s the perfect place to end your trip.

While Barcelona tends to get more attention, I think Madrid is one of the best cities in Europe. It boasts a mouthwatering culinary scene, a raucous nightlife, and tons of things to see and do — no matter your interest or budget. I’ve been visiting the city for almost two decades and never get tired of the tapas, architecture, and history. The city just packs so much in and there really is something for everyone here. By following the itinerary above, you’ll see all the main sights while also getting off the beaten path in Spain’s historic capital.

沃什的表态迅速带动市场重新定价。交易员将本月美联储加息的押注概率从周四的逾25%降至15%。美元指数下跌0.1%，此前一个交易日已累计下挫0.3%，创逾一个月最大单日跌幅。亚太股市和欧洲股市随之走高，美股期货亦小幅上涨。


DBS Bank宏观策略师Wei Liang Chang指出，"市场对沃什重申AI将在中期提振生产率的判断感到宽慰，这有助于缓和通胀预期，并压低连续加息的担忧。"


欧洲斯托克50指数涨0.4%，德国DAX指数涨0.5%，法国CAC 40指数涨0.3%，英国富时100指数则小幅下跌0.4%。

加息预期松动，风险资产获喘息空间

Saxo Markets首席投资策略师Charu Chanana表示，"沃什拒绝承诺再次加息，导致部分美联储加息押注被平仓。在强劲通胀数据公布后，他表示'不会预判会议结果'，这一措辞对美元构成压制。"


美联储于9月上调利率25个基点，为2023年以来首次加息，并获全部19名政策委员一致支持，多数委员亦预计年内可能再度加息。此后数周，多位官员重申可能需要进一步紧缩，但强调有足够时间收集经济数据再行决策。


芯片股止跌，亚欧市场普遍上涨

在沃什讲话之前，全球股市已因芯片股抛售潮趋缓而率先走高。亚洲市场方面，三星电子和SK Hynix均涨逾4%，带动韩国首尔综指收涨2%，报5668.05点，从周四跌至4月以来最低收盘价的低谷中反弹。日经225指数收涨1.4%，报65324.29点；日本东证指数收涨1.7%，报4066点。

欧洲市场开盘亦整体偏强，欧洲斯托克50指数涨0.4%，德国DAX指数涨0.5%，法国CAC 40指数涨0.3%，英国富时100指数则小幅下跌0.4%。


值得关注的是，印度尼西亚股市盘中一度暴跌逾11%，创1998年1月以来最大跌幅，原因是MSCI宣布将印尼从新兴市场指数中剔除，印尼盾亦小幅走低。

反弹持续性存疑，科技板块集中风险犹存

黄金价格基本持平于每盎司4172美元。布伦特原油下跌0.7%，报每桶105.20美元，油价高企持续为通胀预期提供支撑——中东冲突爆发以来，油价一直是美国通胀顽固维持高位的重要推手。

此轮股市反弹能否延续，在一定程度上取决于涨势能否从主导今年大部分升幅的科技重仓股扩散至更广泛的板块。本周的剧烈波动暴露了市场过度依赖AI概念股的风险，更广泛的板块参与将有助于降低这种集中度风险。


东洋证券策略师Ryuta Otsuka表示，"目前看来是一次技术性反弹，整体市场情绪有所平复。"他同时提醒，下周随着投资者继续追踪财报数据并"寻底"，市场波动率可能仍维持相对高位。

items.text:
上周五，由英伟达和黑石联合支持的澳大利亚数据中心运营商Firmus，宣布撤回原本将成为澳大利亚史上第二大IPO的上市计划。该公司寻求的估值高达440亿澳元（约305亿美元）——是三个月前一轮融资估值的整整两倍，远超拥有近5亿澳元营收和8200万澳元净利润的成熟同业NextDC的市值。数日后，另一家澳大利亚数据中心公司AirTrunk亦以"市场条件"为由，取消了在新加坡上市REIT载体的计划。


两宗折戟迅速在全球市场激起涟漪。CoreWeave首席执行官Mike Intrator周四在一份内部备忘录中，将公司股价本周累计下跌17%的部分原因归咎于此："Firmus、AirTrunk、Lambda Labs和Nscale等公司的IPO受挫及债务融资困难，正在渗入围绕CoreWeave的市场叙事。"他强调，这些公司试图在缺乏"执行力、营收和规模"的情况下募集巨额资本，与CoreWeave的情况截然不同。


然而，这番辩白并未平息市场疑虑——CoreWeave债券收益率周四仍逼近15%，债券价格跌破80美分困境区间。


Firmus折戟解剖：贪婪、信任崩塌与估值泡沫


Firmus的IPO失败，是一个关于估值失控与信任连续受损的典型案例。


该公司2019年以比特币矿工身份在塔斯马尼亚起步，后转型AI基础设施并获英伟达加持。联合创始人Oliver Curtis因2016年内幕交易被定罪入狱的背景，令部分潜在股东心存疑虑。更关键的是，Firmus寻求的300亿美元估值，是三个月前融资估值的两倍，而其上市后计划举借的最高300亿美元债务，将使债务/EBITDA比率达到2028年预测盈利的6倍。部分超级年金基金（如UniSuper）以估值过高为由直接拒绝参与。


压垮IPO的最后一根稻草，是上市前一周曝光的"Project Southgate"交易破裂——Firmus与CDC之间一笔数十亿美元的合作协议突然告吹，直接动摇了潜在投资者对公司商业落地能力的信心。


投资公司Ten Cap创始人兼首席投资组合经理Jun Bei Liu在摩根斯年度投资会议上直言："他们太贪婪了，应该更现实一些。"承销行摩根士丹利、摩根大通和美国银行均未就撤单公开置评。


Firmus目前表示将转向私募市场融资，但在当前信用环境下，其借贷成本或将大幅上升。与此同时，同样在纳斯达克上市、寻求在澳大利亚二次上市的SharonAI，股价过去五日已下跌近两成——澳大利亚数据中心资本市场的寒意，远未消散。

Firmus折戟不过是引线，真正的火药桶早已埋下。


据英国《金融时报》10月16日报道，为Meta、英伟达、甲骨文等科技巨头提供算力的知名数据中心项目债券价格，近期已全面跌破面值：Blue Owl与Meta联合支持的"Hyperion"项目债券从7月初面值以上跌至约92美分；黑石旗下租赁给微软的佐治亚州QTS"Project Excalibur"债券已跌破88美分；Hut 8开发的路易斯安那州和德克萨斯州项目债券分别跌至约94美分和92美分。甲骨文相关项目承压尤甚——与"Project Jupiter"新墨西哥州数据中心挂钩的约180亿美元贷款因电力许可延误已滑入困境区间，密歇根州AI园区建设债券亦从面值跌至87美分。


neocloud公司受到的冲击更为剧烈。CoreWeave债券已跌破80美分困境门槛，收益率逼近15%，竞争对手Nebius本周跌幅达18%。英伟达过去一周市值蒸发约2700亿美元。


德国安联首席投资官Ludovic Subran将这一局面定性为"达尔文时刻"："电力和施工延误引发的信用利差飙升，表明数据中心债务的定价对执行风险的容忍度过低。"

债券抛售的深层逻辑，是一道始终无解的算术题。

Gartner进一步指出，AI优化IaaS赛道市场规模预计从2027年的660亿美元增至2030年的1740亿美元，但在现有芯片被新一代替代之前，这一体量对大多数AI算力提供商而言仍"不足以收回投资"。更关键的是，由于多数AI原生公司采用轻资产模式，"不足一半的AI收入将流向拥有重大AI基础设施的提供商"。


触发市场情绪转变的另一导火索，是OpenAI的一系列信号：年化营收比此前暗示的数字低出200亿美元，IPO推迟至明年，Anthropic季度销售增速亦在放缓。这些信号共同指向一个令市场不安的结论：AI变现的速度，远远跟不上基础设施投入的节奏。


D.A. Davidson分析师Gil Luria的判断更为直白：CoreWeave借款成本约9%，投资回报率仅约1%。"一旦AI支出热潮降温，股权价值将归零。"


英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋周四表示，他不认为CoreWeave需要英伟达提供支撑，"他们的资本成本实际上正在下降"。但他未提供具体财务数据，而信用市场的定价与这番乐观表态形成了鲜明对比。


两重隐患：循环融资与政治反弹


除营收缺口外，两类结构性风险正在叠加放大这场危机的烈度。


其一是循环融资风险。国际清算银行近期报告指出，"AI领域相当大比例的融资和商业关系具有自我指涉性"——客户与供应商相互为对方融资。这种结构在市场顺风时可放大增长，一旦信心逆转，则可能加速去杠杆并引发连锁反应。


其二是来自地方的政治阻力。针对数据中心的反弹情绪已在美国多地蔓延——纽约、德克萨斯等州已对新项目设置严格限制，部分项目因此停滞。Columbia Threadneedle美国投资级信用主管Tom Murphy表示，这使得"已建成运营的数据中心更具价值"，但同时也意味着新建项目的许可风险被系统性低估。

尽管市场动荡，这场危机的终局或许并非AI基础设施投资的终结，而是一次残酷的优胜劣汰。


Gartner预测，80%的neocloud将在2030年前"停止独立运营"——每五家租用英伟达GPU的公司中，有四家将被并购或退出市场。但与此同时，澳大利亚联邦银行经济学家Lucinda Jerogin指出，澳大利亚数据中心装机容量已从今年2月的约6吉瓦增至23吉瓦，尽管其中仅约四分之一获批或在建，行业的长期成长逻辑并未动摇。


Jun Bei Liu认为，Goodman、AirTrunk等拥有成熟财务支撑和长期协议的成熟企业，以及持有确定合同的建筑和工程公司，仍是值得关注的"真正的宝石"。"它们将继续受益于这一代际性增长，但对于'快速致富'的玩家而言，这条路将越来越难走。"


这正是这场"达尔文时刻"的核心逻辑：在4.9万亿美元的收支鸿沟面前，Firmus式的估值游戏已走到尽头。只有具备真实营收、规模和执行力的运营商，才能在这场淘汰赛中活下来——而那些依赖循环融资、靠故事撑起估值的玩家，正在被市场逐一清算。

低空经济方面，香港发展低空经济工作组正全力制订《发展低空经济规划行动纲领》，明确推动与内地联合设立国际低空经济合作组织、尽快实现跨境低空物流试飞；叠加特斯拉第二代Roadster跑车发布等，推动低空经济概念股爆发。生物医药午后跳水，药明康德尾盘一度跌停，中国基金报称，药明康德在市场上出现了一篇小作文，搅动了市场情绪。不过有业内人士表示，这是去年三月份的谣言又重新传播。

10月16日，A股在隔夜外围企稳、美股三大指数收涨的背景下集体高开，三大指数一度均涨超1%，午后震荡回落、尾盘加速下行，创业板指一度跌超1%，尾盘部分宽基ETF再度放量，其中沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞成交超110亿元，上证50ETF华夏成交超30亿，沪指小幅收涨。

板块方面，低空经济、通用航空、军工信息化、国防军工、商业航天等概念股集体爆发，航天军工、房地产、汽车等板块走高，江淮汽车涨停，此前工信部等三部门成立联合调查组开展核查网络反映的“尊界V800汽车刹车踏板支架断裂问题”。此外，AI硬件午后回落下跌，光模块下挫，电路板、覆铜板陷入调整。创新药跳水，CRO大幅下跌，药明康德跌停，凯莱英等跟跌。

港股全天震荡上涨，午后回吐部分涨幅，恒指仍收涨，恒科指涨超1%，此前一度涨2%，权重科网股集体反弹，联想、阿里、京东、腾讯、网易、百度等涨幅居前。AI大模型股、光模块、芯片半导体等集体走高。债市方面，国债期货全线反弹。商品方面，国内商品期货涨跌不一。

A股：截至收盘，沪指涨0.24%，深成指跌0.12%，创业板指跌0.39%。

盘面上，个股涨多跌少，沪深京三市超3200股飘红，今日成交1.57万亿。沪深两市成交额1.56万亿，较上一个交易日缩量超700亿。板块方面，化纤、军工、地产、汽车、农业板块全天强势，覆铜板、传媒、半导体板块午后走软，药明康德触及跌停拖累创新药方阵，尾盘银行、保险、煤炭等红利资产出手护盘。

港股：截至收盘，恒指涨0.52%，恒科指涨1.16%。

飞行汽车概念全线爆发，北交所捷众科技30%涨停，华力创通、佳力奇、金盾股份、广联航空、 英搏尔皆20%涨停，整个板块暴涨超5%。

分析人士认为，当地时间10月15日，特斯拉正式发布Roadster电动超跑。这可能是引爆行情的关键所在。马斯克在开场时表示：“你将看到世界最好的汽车公司与世界最好的火箭公司合作的结果。”这一表述奠定了整场活动的基调：Roadster不仅是一辆电动超跑，还被特斯拉包装为汽车工程与SpaceX火箭技术交叉的产物。

目前，特斯拉美国官网已开放Roadster预订，Performance版本的预订意向金为5万美元，其中首笔支付5000美元，剩余4.5万美元须在10天内支付；Thrust版本的预订意向金则达到25万美元，其中首笔支付5000美元，剩余24.5万美元须在10天内支付。Rocket版本目前仅接受邀请预订。

特斯拉中国官网也已开放Roadster预订，与美国官网不同，中国官网目前仅开放Performance版本预订，预订意向金为33.2万元人民币。

items.text:
10 月 2 日，苹果做了一件很少见的事，因为一个第三方 App，宣布要调整系统规则。


起因是《Inc.》杂志的科技专栏作者 Jason Aten 公开指控，Meta 的 AI 智能体 Muse 在他的 Mac 上读取了私人消息。Muse 是 Meta 力推的「能替你办事」的 Agent，会帮你退订闲置会员，甚至替你砍价。


苹果随即表态，今后 AI 请求读取 Mac 数据时，系统会主动提示用户。


这几乎就是苹果和 Meta 过去五年关系的缩影，Meta 想拿数据，苹果出面拦着。


然而仅仅两周后，故事发生了反转。


当地时间 10 月 15 日，Meta 发布开放权重模型 Muse Spark Open，扎克伯格在 X 上发帖，感谢「John Ternus 和苹果」的合作，让这个模型能在新款 Mac Studio 上流畅运行。


苹果 CEO Ternus 本人很快回复，称能在自己桌上如此高效地跑起这种量级的模型：


「鹅妹子嘤」。


Meta 的 AI 负责人 Alexandr Wang 接受 Axios 采访时，说了一句更搞笑但直白的话：


「很高兴爸爸妈妈又和好了。」


所以，「爸爸」和「妈妈」，是怎么和好的？以及，Meta 最近连续在模型上发力，终于重回牌桌了吗？


01 一台桌子，放下 8000 亿参数


先看这次苹果和 Meta 的合作到底做成了什么。


Meta 宣称 Muse Spark Open 总参数 8160 亿，每次推理只激活其中 420 亿，支持 100 万 token 的上下文。Meta 称它是：


「迄今美国最强的开放权重模型」。


注意这个措辞里的「美国」两个字。论参数规模，它并不是全球最大的开源模型。月之暗面的 Kimi K2、蚂蚁的 Ling-1T，早在 2025 年就把开源模型推到了万亿参数级别。Meta 这次是在追赶，而且对手是中国公司。


真正新鲜的，是它跑在哪里。

苹果的 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 绝对是本地模型利器｜图片来源：Apple


按 Meta 的说法，两台顶配 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 就能装下整个模型。每台 Mac Studio 的 GPU 能直接调用最多 512GB 统一内存，两台连起来约 1TB，在 Apple 的 MLX 框架下像一台小型超算一样协同工作。


这件事放在别的 AI 硬件平台上，几乎不可能放在一张书桌上。


道理不复杂。这类「总参数大、激活参数小」的模型，最需要的是超大的内存容量，对带宽的要求反倒没那么极端。每生成一个 token，模型只需要读取 420 亿参数那一小块，M5 Ultra 每秒 1.2TB 的内存带宽足够应付。


换到 NVIDIA 阵营，一张消费级显卡的显存不过几十 GB，想装下 8000 亿参数，得上 8 卡 H100 级别的服务器，那是机房里的设备，不是桌面上的。


也就是说，苹果统一内存架构这几年被嘲笑「贵」的那部分，恰好成了跑超大模型的护城河。


Meta 展示的用例也很有针对性。基于 Muse Spark Open 的编程工具 Muse Code，全程在本地完成了两件事。一件是给开源 Mastodon 客户端 Ice Cubes 提交 iOS 代码修改，另一件是操作 DaVinci Resolve 审看素材，把横屏视频裁成竖屏。


写代码、剪视频，两个都是 Mac 用户最典型的工作场景。


当然，门槛也很现实。256GB 内存版的 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 起售价已经是 10799 美元，512GB 版本预计本月晚些时候才上市，两台下来价格可想而知。这不是给普通消费者准备的，而是给开发者、工作室和对数据敏感的企业准备的。


02「爸爸」「妈妈」怎么和好了？


要理解苹果和 Meta 这次握手有多不寻常，得把时间往回拨。


2021 年，苹果在 iOS 14.5 推出「App 跟踪透明度」，App 想跨应用追踪用户，必须先弹窗征得同意。绝大多数用户选择了拒绝。Meta 后来在财报会上承认，这项政策让它 2022 年损失约 100 亿美元收入。


其实，两家的梁子结得比这更早。


2018 年剑桥分析丑闻后，库克公开说苹果「不会陷入这种境地」，扎克伯格回击这番话「极其轻率」。2019 年，苹果吊销了 Facebook 的企业开发者证书，起因是 Facebook 借此分发一款收集用户数据的研究 App，一度导致 Facebook 内部所有测试版 App 集体瘫痪。


到了 2024 年，扎克伯格在播客里吐槽苹果「已经很久没发明出什么伟大的东西了」。同一年，《华尔街日报》报道两家曾讨论把 Llama 接入 Apple Intelligence，但彭博社的 Mark Gurman 随后透露，苹果早就因为隐私顾虑放弃了这条路。


按 MacDailyNews 的说法，两家上一次公开合作，大约要追溯到 2017 年。


是什么让坚冰化开？

库克时代的苹果曾经和 Meta 结下很深的梁子｜图片来源：Reddit


第一个答案是人。


苹果的掌舵人已经换成 John Ternus，那个和扎克伯格隔空对骂多年的库克，不再坐在 CEO 的位置上。另一个关键人物是 Daniel Gross，他早年把自己的创业公司卖给苹果，在苹果负责过机器学习，2025 年加入 Meta 的超级智能团队。据报道，这次合作正是他在中间牵线。


第二个答案，也是更根本的答案，就是是两家公司都在 AI 上有求于对方。


先看苹果。


外媒对这次合作的定性毫不客气，称这是苹果在自研模型落后之后，又一次寻找比自己更强的模型伙伴，希望用 AI 功能拉动硬件需求。


在此之前，苹果已经把 OpenAI 和 Google 的模型接进了 Siri 和 Apple Intelligence。但那两家走的都是云端路线，苹果只是一个入口。


Meta 给了苹果一个只有 Mac 才能讲的故事，前沿级别的 AI，在用户自己的桌上跑，数据不出门。


这和苹果多年来的隐私叙事严丝合缝，也正好为一款即将上市、售价不菲的 512GB Mac Studio 做了最好的预热。


再看 Meta。


Alexandr Wang 说得很坦白，Muse Spark Open 并不是 Meta 最强的模型，它的任务是吸引开发者，让他们先在小范围内试起来，再往上扩展。


开放权重模型的生命线是开发者生态，而写代码的人，桌上放的很多是 Mac。据报道，Meta 今年早些时候还采购了数百台 Mac 用于内部 AI 实验，这个判断显然不是临时起意。


但 Meta 也没有把鸡蛋放在苹果一个篮子里。Muse Spark Open 的权重同步上架了亚马逊、谷歌、微软三家云平台，从 SGLang、vLLM 到 llama.cpp 主流推理框架全部支持，还专门为 AMD MI350 做了内核优化。


苹果是这张网里最上镜的一个节点，但 Meta 要的是一张谁都绕不开的网。


03 Meta 重回牌桌？


把时间线拉长，这次握手只是 Meta 一连串密集动作的一环。


1 年多前的 2025 年 4 月，Llama 4 发布后陷入跑分争议，口碑一落千丈。两个月后，扎克伯格豪掷 143 亿美元投资 Scale AI，把 Alexandr Wang 请来组建超级智能实验室，又开出天价薪酬四处挖人。


一年多过去，「Llama」这个名字被「Muse」取代。今年 9 月的 Connect 大会，Meta 发布了个人 AI 产品 Muse。10 月 2 日，面向 Agent 的 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full 上线，主打跨对话的个人记忆，以及在长任务中不断换思路、自我检查的能力。几天后，就是这次的 Muse Spark Open。


闭源旗舰、消费级 Agent、开放权重，三条线在同一个月里齐头并进。

此次 Meta Spark Open 的一些测试结果｜图片来源：Meta


按 Meta 自己的说法，Muse Wonder Full 在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数上排名第二，只比 Claude Opus 5.5 低两分。


但「回来了」和「崛起」之间，还有一段距离。


Muse Spark Open 的博客里还没有给出具体跑分，完整评测报告写的是「即将发布」。MacRumors 这篇合作报道下面，排在前列的读者评论几乎一边倒地表达对 Meta 的不信任。而那个读私人消息的指控，Meta 虽然否认，却已经逼得苹果出面调整规则。


Meta 的技术或许追上来了，信任却还欠着账。


这也是这次合作最微妙的地方。一边是苹果为了防 Meta 的 Agent 给系统加上新的提示，一边是苹果 CEO 亲自为 Meta 的模型点赞。


两件事并不矛盾。苹果拦的是 Meta 伸向用户数据的手，欢迎的是 Meta 放进 Mac 里的模型，前者威胁苹果的隐私招牌，后者帮苹果卖硬件。


19 世纪的英国首相帕默斯顿说过，没有永恒的盟友，也没有永恒的敌人，只有永恒的利益。


在 AI 这张牌桌上，苹果缺模型，Meta 缺入口，这份利益，足够让「爸爸妈妈」暂时坐到同一张桌子前。


至于会不会一直和好下去，两家公司的发言人显然也给不出确切的答案。

开放权重模型的生命线是开发者生态，而写代码的人，桌上放的很多是 Mac。据报道，Meta 今年早些时候还采购了数百台 Mac 用于内部 AI 实验，这个判断显然不是临时起意。
但 Meta 也没有把鸡蛋放在苹果一个篮子里。Muse Spark Open 的权重同步上架了亚马逊、谷歌、微软三家云平台，从 SGLang、vLLM 到 llama.cpp 主流推理框架全部支持，还专门为 AMD MI350 做了内核优化。
苹果是这张网里最上镜的一个节点，但 Meta 要的是一张谁都绕不开的网。
03 Meta 重回牌桌？
把时间线拉长，这次握手只是 Meta 一连串密集动作的一环。
1 年多前的 2025 年 4 月，Llama 4 发布后陷入跑分争议，口碑一落千丈。两个月后，扎克伯格豪掷 143 亿美元投资 Scale AI，把 Alexandr Wang 请来组建超级智能实验室，又开出天价薪酬四处挖人。
一年多过去，「Llama」这个名字被「Muse」取代。今年 9 月的 Connect 大会，Meta 发布了个人 AI 产品 Muse。10 月 2 日，面向 Agent 的 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full 上线，主打跨对话的个人记忆，以及在长任务中不断换思路、自我检查的能力。几天后，就是这次的 Muse Spark Open。
闭源旗舰、消费级 Agent、开放权重，三条线在同一个月里齐头并进。
此次 Meta Spark Open 的一些测试结果｜图片来源：Meta
按 Meta 自己的说法，Muse Wonder Full 在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数上排名第二，只比 Claude Opus 5.5 低两分。
但「回来了」和「崛起」之间，还有一段距离。
Muse Spark Open 的博客里还没有给出具体跑分，完整评测报告写的是「即将发布」。MacRumors 这篇合作报道下面，排在前列的读者评论几乎一边倒地表达对 Meta 的不信任。而那个读私人消息的指控，Meta 虽然否认，却已经逼得苹果出面调整规则。
Meta 的技术或许追上来了，信任却还欠着账。
这也是这次合作最微妙的地方。一边是苹果为了防 Meta 的 Agent 给系统加上新的提示，一边是苹果 CEO 亲自为 Meta 的模型点赞。
两件事并不矛盾。苹果拦的是 Meta 伸向用户数据的手，欢迎的是 Meta 放进 Mac 里的模型，前者威胁苹果的隐私招牌，后者帮苹果卖硬件。
19 世纪的英国首相帕默斯顿说过，没有永恒的盟友，也没有永恒的敌人，只有永恒的利益。
在 AI 这张牌桌上，苹果缺模型，Meta 缺入口，这份利益，足够让「爸爸妈妈」暂时坐到同一张桌子前。
至于会不会一直和好下去，两家公司的发言人显然也给不出确切的答案。

items.title: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow
items.summary: The number of ships that have reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz has hit a record high, BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime
items.text:
The number of ships that have reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz has hit a record high, BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime agency shows.

Twelve vessels were attacked between 5 and 11 October - the largest number of weekly strikes reported to the UK's Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw 10 ships reporting attacks.

Six of the vessels were struck last Sunday, according to the UKMTO - a one-day high. So far this week, there have been four reported attacks.

As the number of strikes has risen, the recovery in oil shipments through the strait seen last month has slowed, industry data suggests.

BBC Verify collated incident reports published by the UKMTO on its website and created a timeline based on the first date cited in each report. This is approximate because some incidents use the date of the attack and some the date on which it was reported.

Experts say Tehran has been attacking ships in an effort to assert greater control over the waterway as the US military has increased the number of tankers it is shepherding through the south of the strait to evade Iranian strikes.

Iran is also carrying out more attacks on vessels further away from the Strait of Hormuz, according to experts.

The US military's Central Command, which oversees operations in the Middle East, posted on social media that despite the attacks "commercial traffic continues to flow through the Strait of Hormuz with co-ordinated protection from US forces and regional partners".

The aftermath of one of Sunday's six reported attacks was captured in verified footage showing the Nicaragua-flagged tanker Petro Dolphin on fire, as filmed by the crew on a smaller boat nearby.

The vessel was struck by a drone close to the Sohar Anchorage, Oman, more than 250km (150 miles) from the strait, according to the maritime intelligence firm Vanguard.

Eleven Indian seafarers were rescued but two are still missing, the Forward Seamen's Union of India said.

Attacks have continued this week with the container ship GFS Pride sinking after a strike by an unknown projectile in the strait on Tuesday. Twenty-one crew were safely evacuated.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) published footage of what appeared to be the same ship sinking. It said the vessel was carrying "2,500 containers of contraband" and had taken an "unauthorised route".

Middle East oil exports have slowed as the number of ship strikes has risen.

About 12.6 million barrels per day went through the strait on 13 October, below the 15 million reported at the end of September, data from trade intelligence firm Kpler shows. This compares with a pre-war baseline of some 17 million barrels per day.

The recent increase in attacks comes as US Navy data indicates the number of vessels given assistance to navigate the Strait of Hormuz during the first 10 days of October was up 85% compared with the same period in August.

Most of the oil being shipped from Gulf Arab states recently has been carried using a "shuttle" system where a fleet of tankers load up and sail through the strait before transferring their cargo to larger tankers in the Gulf of Oman.

These shuttle ships use a route close to Oman's coastline. Iran says this is "unauthorised" and insist vessels take an alternative route closer to its own shore.

So-called assisted transits were a key factor in helping drive oil flows from the Middle East back towards pre-war levels in September. This does not include Iranian exports which have completely stalled as a result of the US blockade of Iranian ports and ships.

Martin Kelly, CEO of Orbital Risk Intelligence, said Iran has "evolved its strategy" in response to this loosening of its control over the strait and has been carrying out "near daily or multiple attacks every single day".

"The aim here is to stop the ships going through and to deter others," he added.

The IRGC's navy has said strikes would not be "limited to the Strait of Hormuz" and later announced a "new deployment formation" across the region, according to state media.

Martin Kelly told BBC Verify that Iran is widening its attacks and targeting ships near the coast of Gulf Arab states and in the Gulf of Oman.

A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles north of Qatar on Thursday 8 October, more than 500km (310 miles) from the strait, resulting in multiple reported casualties, according to Vanguard.

Another tanker was attacked close to the UAE town of Al-Jazirah al-Hamra on Friday 9 October, Vanguard said.

Verified footage shows crew members running across the deck and putting on lifejackets as a large cloud of black smoke rises over the ship.

items.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
items.summary:
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.

Trump had previously
items.text:
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.

Trump had previously said he approved of showing the death of the Fort Hood attacker, while Vice-President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would happen and said he would not watch it.

Trump's decision to cancel the livestream came after widespread criticism in the US and globally. On Thursday, he said that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die".

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan," Trump said.

"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," the president added in the post on Truth Social.

Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US military personnel and injured 32 others at a military base in Texas in 2009. His execution by firing squad will be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Trump said the families of the victims can still view the execution in person if they wish.

"They deserve to witness JUSTICE!" he said.

After the Pentagon announced last week that it would execute Hasan on 3 December 2026 by firing squad and livestream the event, a cascade of criticism quickly followed from human rights groups and many others. The United Nations called the plans "abhorrent".

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. According to Amnesty International, 11 public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth defended his decision to air Hasan's execution online, saying that "people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things".

But as criticism mounted, Trump appeared to hedge his support, saying on Friday that he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan, but adding that the Pentagon was still "making a determination" on it.

The president also called Hasan "totally nuts".

"I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes, and I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him," he said.

After Trump announced he called it off, a Pentagon spokesman said Hegseth had spoken with the US president beforehand.

"The Secretary supports the President's decision, and they are completely aligned," the spokesman Sean Parnell said.

John Galligan, a lawyer for Hasan working primarily on civil issues, told the BBC that Trump's decision to cancel the livestream of his execution "comes as no surprise".

"It was initially a dumb decision and statement by Hegseth to livestream any execution - and it violated the Army's own regulation," Galligan said.

He said Hasan is paralysed from the chest down, something that Trump "allegedly didn't even know" when he approved the livestream plan.

"The damage has already been done - the Army is now just trying to clean up the mess," Galligan said. "It will permanently remain a stain on our military justice system."

He added that it was not clear if Hasan was aware yet of Trump's "reversal" of the livestream decision.

Hasan opened fire in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

He later admitted in court that he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes".

He said during his court martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

US military law requires that a military execution be approved by the US president.

It also requires appellate review, when a higher court inspects the decision and gives a final judgement on its legality to move forward.

Today, we’re
items.text:
Muse Spark Open is available today and brings leading agentic capabilities to your desktop for the first time on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Today, we’re releasing the weights for Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window. Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

We believe the future is for everyone, and that includes the freedom to run advanced models wherever, including at home. Muse Spark Open is the first model in its class to run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.

Muse Spark Open is available today through API platforms at Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Model weights are available for download on Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models.

It runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon. Developers can easily further customize the model using the PyTorch framework.

Key Benchmarks

For more details about our evaluations, see the evaluation methodology report.

Optimized for Apple Silicon

Leveraging the latest version of MLX, Muse Spark Open was optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra's integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS changes to Ice Cubes (an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.

Available Now

We’re sharing this work because we want everyone to have access to the best models. The open-weight version of Muse Spark ships with custom, auto-tunable Helion GPU kernels in SGLang, delivering 1.03-3.95× kernel-level speedups on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and a 3% end-to-end speedup on AMD MI350.

Safety and Preparedness

Releasing open-weight models is part of how we bring the benefits of personal superintelligence to everyone, and part of how safety work advances across the field.

Open weights also carry their own considerations, and Muse Spark Open has additional safety post-training for that reason. The results demonstrate strong safeguards across risk categories measured.

We evaluated the model in line with our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework, covering the most severe risks, and it met the thresholds our framework requires for release. Detailed results are in the Muse Spark Open model card, with a full evaluation report available soon.

License

We’re releasing the weights under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free.

Get Started

You can customize Muse Spark Open for your use case by leveraging PyTorch’s TorchTitan to further tune the model. To run it on Apple silicon, use MLX, which pulls the weights directly from Hugging Face.

Muse Spark Open is available now through Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-spark-open

Built or published something with Muse Spark Open? Share with us on the Hugging Face Forums — we’d love to see what you create.

It runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon. Developers can easily further customize the model using the PyTorch framework.

Optimized for Apple Silicon
Leveraging the latest version of MLX, Muse Spark Open was optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra's integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS changes to Ice Cubes (an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.
Available Now

We’re sharing this work because we want everyone to have access to the best models. The open-weight version of Muse Spark ships with custom, auto-tunable Helion GPU kernels in SGLang, delivering 1.03-3.95× kernel-level speedups on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and a 3% end-to-end speedup on AMD MI350.
Safety and Preparedness
Releasing open-weight models is part of how we bring the benefits of personal superintelligence to everyone, and part of how safety work advances across the field.
Open weights also carry their own considerations, and Muse Spark Open has additional safety post-training for that reason. The results demonstrate strong safeguards across risk categories measured.

We evaluated the model in line with our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework, covering the most severe risks, and it met the thresholds our framework requires for release. Detailed results are in the Muse Spark Open model card, with a full evaluation report available soon.
